newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica all-share hits fresh high, industrials sag.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica all-share hits fresh high, industrials sag.

text.p: The South African all share index climbed to a fresh high at the close of a mixed trading day on Tuesday, dealers said.
The index rose 30.1 points to 7,203.2 from a previous record high of 7,152.0 on Monday against a backdrop of a stronger rand and generally upbeat sentiment, dealers said.
Golds moved higher on the back of a steady bullion price, dealers said. The index finished 9.2 points up at 1,538.5.
Industrials, which at the start of trade looked bullish, were tamed towards the close by losses in industrial heavyweights Barlow Rand and Sasol.
However, no accurate indication of the closing index could be gleaned from Johannesburg Stock Exchange figures because of an calculating error, the exchange said.
Overall trading volumes on the day were pegged at around 944 million rand.
The March all-share contract ended up 6,590/00 from 6,570, the industrial contract closed up at 8,215/20 from 8,205 and the gold contract down 1,087/95 from 1,094.
Dealers expected Wednesday trade to be bullish but said there was some concern about U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspans's semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony.
